Use TextureView for video rendering to achieve zero-latency blur and lens effects

Container options & Trade-offs
• SurfaceView + PixelCopy (Default)
Video runs in hardware composer mode (HWC) for maximum power efficiency and zero battery burden. However, background capture for liquid glass has minor frame delay.
• TextureView
Enables zero-latency real-time liquid glass blur/refraction, but increases GPU load during video playback.
• ExoPlayer engine note
ExoPlayer's SurfaceView relies on layout constraints for scaling and aspect ratio control, preventing PixelCopy from capturing correct pixel coordinates for real-time blur and lens distortion. Therefore, under ExoPlayer, blur and lens distortion effects are disabled unless TextureView is enabled.

Powerful & Feature-rich. Supports advanced ASS/SSA stylized subtitles, software audio gain, full format decoding, and custom Shader filters.
Native Hardware Decoding. Powered by Android MediaCodec & disk caching. Power-efficient, smooth, and stable for standard video playback.
Prioritize performance and lower power consumption. Recommended for most mobile devices.
The default mpv configuration. Balanced settings for most content.
Enable high-quality scaling and debanding filters. May increase power consumption and heat.
An alias for high-quality, specifically tuned for modern GPUs.
Optimize for minimal playback delay. Ideal for live streams or gaming content.
Fastest software decoding profile. Use if hardware acceleration is unavailable.
Manually configure scaling and debanding instead of using profile presets
The output driver used for video rendering
Standard GPU renderer. Highly stable and compatible.
New experimental renderer based on libplacebo. Supports more advanced features.
Graphics API used by the renderer
Default graphics API. Fast and widely supported.
Modern, low-overhead graphics API. May provide better performance on supported hardware.
Policy for hardware accelerated video decoding
Directly render frames to an Android Surface. Best performance and efficiency.
Copy decoded frames back to system memory. Allows post-processing by mpv but is slower.
Use the CPU for decoding. Slowest, but avoids hardware bugs.
How the player synchronizes audio and video
Time video frames to audio. Robust mode with no display assumptions; may drop or repeat frames.
Resample audio to match display refresh rate, automatically compensating for drift.
Resample audio and drop video frames to compensate for drift.
Like Display Resample, but apply speed changes to audio filters to avoid pitch changes.
Drop or repeat video frames to compensate for desyncing video.
Drop or repeat audio data to compensate for desyncing video.
Sync video to display and let audio play independently.
Reduces ringing and halo artifacts during scaling
Bilinear hardware texture filtering (fastest, very low quality). Default for fast profile.
Spline36 scaling. High-quality mid-range algorithm, sharp and reasonably fast.
Elliptic weighted average Lanczos scaling. Relatively slow, but very good quality.
Lanczos scaling. Provides good balance between quality and performance.
A slightly sharpened version of EWA Lanczos. Default for high-quality profile.
Very sharp scaler, prone to ringing. Enables built-in anti-ringing on gpu-next.
Piecewise cubic filter. Provides a balanced compromise of all scaling artifacts.
Hermite spline. Very fast but prone to blocking.
Sharper than Mitchell, but prone to ringing.
Naively oversamples pixels to remove judder artifacts, adding some blur.
Reduce color banding artifacts in the video
The number of debanding steps to perform per sample. Higher values reduce more banding but cost more performance. (Default 1)
The filter\'s cut-off threshold. Higher values increase strength but diminish details. (Default 48)
The filter\'s initial radius. Higher radius finds more gradients, lower radius smooths more aggressively. (Default 16)
Add extra noise to cover up remaining artifacts. (Default 32)
